title: Desktop WebSocket handler blocks the shared event loop on SQLite and audit locks, so one desktop connect stalls every HTTP route
description: The async route /sandboxes/{sid}/desktop/ws (api.py:408-418) and desktop_ws.relay make synchronous SQLite, threading.Lock and Docker SDK calls directly on the asyncio event loop: session lookup, the log_human audit write, vnc_command (_rec + containers.get), the per-message touch(), the 30 s session re-check and the disconnect audit write. While another SQLite connection holds the write lock (retention.prune's BEGIN IMMEDIATE) or a worker holds AuditLog._lock or DesktopControl._lock, a single desktop WS connect or disconnect freezes the whole control plane: every route, including human approvals and deletes, agent tool responses and /healthz, for up to the 5 s busy timeout or the remaining lock hold. A desktop-link session scoped to one sandbox can repeat this by reconnecting, and the desktop page itself auto-reconnects 1.5 s after a server close. An unauthenticated upgrade with any junk cookie also stalls the loop when DesktopControl._lock is held by a worker that is waiting on a SQLite write. This undoes the design intent at api.py:158-160, which isolates blocking work so it cannot stop the human API.
root_cause: desktop_ws (api.py:410-418) and relay (desktop_ws.py:20-21,41,57,72,91) call blocking functions without run_in_threadpool: DesktopControl.session_scope (desktop.py:152-160), AgentBox.log_human / log_best_effort -> AuditLog.append (BEGIN IMMEDIATE under AuditLog._lock, default 5 s busy timeout; audit.py:259,292-296), SandboxManager._rec / containers.get (sandbox.py:185-186,230) and DesktopControl.touch/add_conn. DesktopControl also holds its in-memory _lock across SQLite writes (desktop.py:113-115,120-127,135-139,197-198,204), so the event loop inherits any SQLite write wait that a worker thread is in.
intended_behavior: The event loop never waits on SQLite, threading locks held across I/O, or the Docker daemon. A slow or locked database, or a slow audit read, should only delay the request that needs it, and should never delay unrelated HTTP and WebSocket traffic or responses for other sandboxes.

trace.description: Async WebSocket route; the cookie comes from the upgrade request.
box.desktop.session(cookie, sid) is called synchronously on the event loop.
Takes threading.Lock _lock, which workers hold across SQLite writes (new_session/take/release), and blocks the loop thread while it waits.
vnc_command -> _rec (SandboxManager._lock + SQLite) and containers.get (Docker HTTP) on the loop.
Under AuditLog._lock, BEGIN IMMEDIATE waits up to the default 5 s busy timeout for the write lock, and the whole event loop is blocked during the wait.

evidence.description: The disconnect audit write (log_best_effort) also runs on the loop in finally, so closing a tab stalls the loop too.
touch() takes DesktopControl._lock on the loop for every client message in control mode.
prune holds the SQLite write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) for its whole delete transaction.
verify() reads the whole audit table under AuditLog._lock; recent() (audit.py:311-316) does an unindexed COUNT(*) under the same lock, polled every 3 s by the sandbox page.
Comment states the design intent: blocking tool work is kept off shared execution so the agent cannot freeze the human API.
new_session holds _lock across DELETE+INSERT, so it waits the busy timeout while holding the lock the loop needs.

conditions.description: For the 5 s audit stall: a valid desktop-link session (scope one sandbox) or a full UI session. For the DesktopControl._lock stall: none (any cookie value).

A concurrent long holder must exist: retention.prune's BEGIN IMMEDIATE on the same DB (operator maintenance), a worker inside AuditLog._lock (verify/recent over a large, agent-grown table), or a human desktop write (login/ticket/takeover/handback) that is waiting on the SQLite write lock.
The stall length is bounded by the 5 s default sqlite busy timeout for each write attempt, or by the remaining audit-lock hold, which grows linearly with audit rows.

execution.attacker_perspective: A holder of a desktop link (scoped human session), or just an open desktop tab that auto-reconnects, connects to the desktop WebSocket while another SQLite connection holds the write lock or a worker holds the audit lock.
payloads: /home/user/agentbox/docs/security-audit/run-5/tools/sbx h-ws /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/h.py (h.py: real agentbox.api.build() app with docker.from_env replaced by an in-process fake; dummy human token hum_ddd..., sandbox sb_x template desktop, desktop-link session from box.desktop.new_session('sb_x'))
instructions: Ran in the parent-approved sandbox (no network, no Docker, uid 65534, 512 MiB, 120 s), with AGENTBOX_HOME=/scratch/home, AGENTBOX_DOCKER_CLI=/bin/false and AGENTBOX_MIN_FREE=0.

For each scenario, started a contention holder in a thread: (a) a second sqlite3 connection running BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 7 s, (b) a worker inside AuditLog._lock for 4 s, or (c) BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus a worker calling box.desktop.new_session().
Opened TestClient.websocket_connect('/sandboxes/sb_x/desktop/ws?mode=view') with the link-session cookie, a junk cookie or no cookie, then 0.3 s later timed GET /healthz on the same app.
execution.observed_result: Baseline healthz 0.0 s. Link-session WS under the write lock: healthz 4.72 s, WS closed 1011 after 5.02 s. Junk/no cookie under the write lock: 0.0 s. Junk cookie while new_session waited on the write lock: healthz 4.41 s. Link-session WS while AuditLog._lock was held 4 s: healthz 3.53 s. Junk cookie under the audit lock: 0.0 s.

remediation.strategy: Move every blocking call in desktop_ws/relay off the event loop (run_in_threadpool, or the dedicated pool for audit writes), and stop holding DesktopControl._lock across SQLite I/O by using a separate DB lock, so that touch/add_conn/lease never wait on a database. Regression test: while a second connection holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE, or a thread holds AuditLog._lock, a desktop WS connect must leave GET /healthz latency under 0.5 s.

code_changes.fixed_code:
@app.websocket("/sandboxes/{sid}/desktop/ws")
    async def desktop_ws(ws: WebSocket, sid: str, mode: str = "view"):
        cookie = ws.cookies.get(D.COOKIE)
        if mode not in ("view", "control") or not same_origin(ws.headers) or not cookie:
            await ws.close(code=4401)
            return
        session = await run_in_threadpool(box.desktop.session, cookie, sid)
        if not session:
            await ws.close(code=4401)
            return
        if not await run_in_threadpool(box.desktop.may_connect, sid, session, mode):
            await ws.close(code=4403)
            return
        await relay(ws, box, sid, session, mode, cookie)

try:
        argv = await run_in_threadpool(box.sandboxes.vnc_command, sid, mode == "view")
        await run_in_threadpool(box.log_human, "desktop_connect", sid, {"session": session, "mode": mode})
    except (SandboxError, ServiceError):
        ...
    # session_watch: if not await run_in_threadpool(box.desktop.session, cookie, sid): ...
    # finally: schedule box.log_best_effort(...) on a worker thread (e.g. loop.run_in_executor) instead of calling it inline

# keep self._lock for the in-memory dicts only; guard self._db with a separate self._db_lock,
# and never take self._db_lock while holding self._lock, so touch()/lease()/add_conn() never wait on SQLite

likelihood.reason: Needs a concurrent long SQLite/audit lock holder (operator prune, a human audit view over a large table, or a human desktop write during such a hold) to coincide with a desktop WS event. A desktop-link holder can repeat connects, but cannot create the lock hold itself.

impact.reason: Temporary freeze of all control-plane HTTP/WS traffic (observed 3.5-4.7 s per event, repeatable by reconnecting while the condition lasts). No data or authority gain.

confidence.reason: The event-loop stall was observed with real handler, audit and SQLite code in the sandbox. Real prune durations and Docker daemon latency were not measured (Docker was faked).
